headline_marked: Over 50 injured as [[Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash]] at Dhaka Alia Madrasa
headline: Over 50 injured as Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash at Dhaka Alia Madrasa
summary: Activists from both groups fought over dormitory control, leaving the principal injured and causing significant property damage.
details: Clashes broke out between Chhatra Dal and Islami Chhatra Shibir activists at Dhaka Alia Madrasa on Tuesday, leaving more than 55 people injured.
The violence centered around the control of the Allama Kashgari (R) Hall, with both sides engaging in multiple rounds of fighting throughout the day.
By 6:30 PM, Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal activists reportedly took control of the hall, where they carried out vandalism and assaulted the principal, Mohammad Obaidul Haque.
Reports indicate that 25 members of Chhatra Shibir and over 30 members of Chhatra Dal were injured during the confrontations.
Following the takeover, a Chhatra Dal leader, Md. Ibrahim, locked the hall, citing the need to ensure the safety of the students.
The unrest at the madrasa is part of a wider pattern of clashes between the two student wings in various educational institutions across the capital.
caption:

headline_marked: DMP [[tightens security across Dhaka]] for July Mass Uprising Day
headline: DMP tightens security across Dhaka for July Mass Uprising Day
summary: Increased police pickets, checkposts, and specialized units like SWAT and the Dog Squad are deployed to ensure safety during the anniversary.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has significantly ramped up security across the capital to mark the second anniversary of July Uprising Day.
Security measures include an increase in police pickets and checkposts, particularly at the entry points of Dhaka city.

Specialized units including the Detective Branch (DB), Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, SWAT, the Bomb Disposal Unit, and the Dog Squad are conducting sweeping operations at key venues.
Surveillance has been enhanced using CCTV cameras and drones, while Quick Response Teams remain on standby to handle any emergencies.
Additional personnel from Rab and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) have also been deployed to support the security operations.
At metro rail stations, 50 Armed Police Battalion (APBN) personnel have been deployed across 10 of the 16 stations to prevent sabotage and ensure passenger safety.
The DB Chief stated that while there is no specific threat, the DMP remains on high alert to maintain order during the public gatherings.
caption:
Dhaka is on high alert. SWAT, drones, and the Dog Squad are deployed as the city prepares for July Mass Uprising Day.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has significantly ramped up security across the capital to mark the second anniversary of July Uprising Day.

Security measures include an increase in police pickets and checkposts, particularly at the entry points of Dhaka city.

Specialized units including the Detective Branch (DB), Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, SWAT, the Bomb Disposal Unit, and the Dog Squad are conducting sweeping operations at key venues.

Surveillance has been enhanced using CCTV cameras and drones, while Quick Response Teams remain on standby to handle any emergencies.

Additional personnel from Rab and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) have also been deployed to support the security operations.

At metro rail stations, 50 Armed Police Battalion (APBN) personnel have been deployed across 10 of the 16 stations to prevent sabotage and ensure passenger safety.

The DB Chief stated that while there is no specific threat, the DMP remains on high alert to maintain order during the public gatherings.
